Calculate travel time matrix between origin destination pairs considering a departure time

Source: R/travel_time_matrix.R
travel_time_matrix.Rd

Travel times between every origin and every destination, by one street mode ("WALK", "BICYCLE" or "CAR") or by public transport (all of it or some of its modes), reached by walking, bicycle or car and left by any of them (mode_egress), for departures every minute of a time window. For trips that must arrive by a given time, see arrival_travel_time_matrix(); for each departure of the window on its own, expanded_travel_time_matrix().

Usage

travel_time_matrix(
  network,
  origins,
  destinations,
  mode = "WALK",
  mode_egress = "WALK",
  departure_datetime = NULL,
  time_window = 10L,
  percentiles = 50L,
  max_walk_time = Inf,
  max_bike_time = Inf,
  max_car_time = Inf,
  max_trip_duration = 120L,
  walk_speed = 3.6,
  bike_speed = 12,
  max_rides = 3,
  max_lts = 2,
  fare_structure = NULL,
  max_fare = Inf,
  new_carspeeds = NULL,
  carspeed_scale = 1,
  new_lts = NULL,
  draws_per_minute = 5L,
  seed = NULL,
  n_threads = Inf,
  verbose = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE,
  output_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

network

A network built with build_network().

origins, destinations

A data.frame with columns id, lon and lat (WGS 84 longitude and latitude), or a POINT sf with an id column, in any coordinate reference system (CRS): an sf in another CRS than WGS 84 is reprojected with sf::st_transform(), with a message, and one without a CRS is an error. Ids that are not character are converted, with a warning; points with missing coordinates are not routed, with a warning; duplicated ids are an error.

mode

A character vector, the transport modes (see the section "Transport modes"). Defaults to "WALK".

mode_egress

A string, the mode from the last stop to the destination: "WALK" (the default), "BICYCLE" or "CAR". Ignored without public transport.

departure_datetime

A POSIXct, the departure date and time (see the section "Date and time"). Required with public transport.

time_window

An integer, the number of departure minutes, from departure_datetime on, over which travel times are computed. Defaults to 10.

percentiles

An integer vector of up to 5 values from 1 to 99, the percentiles of the travel time over the departures of the window to report. Defaults to 50, the median.

max_walk_time, max_bike_time, max_car_time

The maximum time in minutes on foot, by bicycle and by car. Each limit applies to each leg on its own (15 minutes to reach the first stop and another 15 from the last), and to the whole trip when that mode is the only one. Inf, the default, leaves only max_trip_duration.

max_trip_duration

An integer, the maximum trip duration in minutes. Defaults to 120.

walk_speed, bike_speed

Average speeds in km/h, 3.6 and 12 by default.

max_rides

An integer, the maximum number of public transport rides in a trip. Defaults to 3.

max_lts

An integer from 1 to 4, the highest level of traffic stress a cyclist rides on (see the section "Level of traffic stress"). Defaults to 2.

fare_structure

A fare structure (see setup_fare_structure()) or NULL (the default): no fares. It must have a row for every route of the network.

max_fare

A number, the highest fare of a trip (Inf, the default: no limit), in the currency of the fare structure; a finite value needs a fare_structure.

new_carspeeds

A scenario of car speeds: NULL (the default), a data frame with columns osm_id, max_speed and speed_type ("scale", a factor for the car speed of the way's edges, or "km/h", a speed; 0 closes the way to cars), or an sf data frame of POLYGONs or MULTIPOLYGONs (in any CRS, reprojected to WGS 84 as origins) with columns poly_id (character), scale (numeric) and priority (integer): each street edge takes the factor of the polygon it meets with the highest priority (ties: the one it overlaps most). Polygons that are not valid are an error, and so is a tie with no winner: two polygons of the same priority and different scales that overlap a way by the same length (give one of them a higher priority).

carspeed_scale

A number of at least 0, the factor for the car speeds of the edges new_carspeeds leaves out (all of them when it is NULL). Defaults to 1. Car speeds are kept as 16-bit centimetres per second: a factor or speed that would bring a speed to 0 or less, or past that range, is an error.

new_lts

A scenario of levels of traffic stress: NULL (the default), a data frame with columns osm_id and lts (integer), or an sf data frame of LINESTRINGs (in any CRS, reprojected to WGS 84 as origins) with columns line_id, lts (1 to 4) and priority: each street edge takes the level of the line closest to it among those whose bounding box meets its own (priority is not used). A scenario (of car speeds or of levels of traffic stress) changes the street search from the origins (the trip without public transport, and access by bicycle or car) but not the egress from the stops, and turns off slope costs, with a warning, on a network built with an elevation raster.

draws_per_minute

An integer, the Monte Carlo draws per departure minute (see the section "Departures and Monte Carlo draws"). Defaults to 5.

seed

An integer seed for the Monte Carlo draws, or NULL (the default: the draws differ from call to call). With a seed, the same inputs give the same results whatever n_threads.

n_threads

The number of threads; Inf (the default) uses all cores (two under R CMD check when it limits the cores).

verbose, progress

Logicals, checked but without effect: no progress counter or routing log is printed.

output_dir

NULL (the default), or the path of an existing directory: instead of returning the result, write it there, one CSV file per origin, from_<origin id>.csv (an id that cannot name a file there, such as one with a path separator, is an error; an existing file of that name is replaced, other files are left alone), and return output_dir. The origins are routed a slice at a time and each slice is written before the next one is routed, so the whole result is never held in memory. The files have the columns of the result (with cutoff also under "fixed_exponential", as the placeholder 0), fields with , or " quoted, NA as an empty field, and doubles in the shortest form that reads back the same, with a decimal point (2.0, 1.0E-4); an origin with no row has no file, except in accessibility(). With output_dir, "WALK" is routed from the origins even when there are fewer destinations, ids must not be missing, and trips over max_trip_duration are not blanked out as in the returned result.

Value

A table with from_id, to_id (character) and one integer column travel_time_pXX per percentile (minutes). Pairs that cannot be completed within max_trip_duration, or whose points are too far from the street network, are not returned; a higher percentile beyond the limit is NA. With output_dir, output_dir.

Tables are tibbles by default; options(peabiru.output = "data.frame") gives base data.frames and options(peabiru.output = "data.table") gives data.tables (see peabiru-package).

Details

A bicycle or car trip to public transport goes on on foot from wherever the vehicle got, within the same max_bike_time or max_car_time (so stops in pedestrian-only areas are reached), and the trip without public transport keeps those walking ends too. Egress by bicycle or car is searched from every stop up to 5 km by bicycle at any level of traffic stress and up to 30 minutes by car, and must stay within max_bike_time or max_car_time.

Transport modes

Street modes: "WALK", "BICYCLE", "CAR". Public transport: "TRANSIT" (every mode) or any of "TRAM", "SUBWAY", "RAIL", "BUS", "FERRY", "CABLE_CAR", "GONDOLA" and "FUNICULAR", which keep only the routes of those 'GTFS' route types. With public transport, the street mode in mode ("WALK" when none is given) is the access mode, used to reach the first stop and, on foot, between stops.

Level of traffic stress

Each street is given a level of traffic stress (LTS) for cyclists from its 'OpenStreetMap' tags: 1 is tolerable for children (quiet streets, separated cycle tracks), 2 for most adults, 3 for confident cyclists, 4 only for the strong and fearless. A cyclist rides only on streets up to max_lts and walks the bicycle elsewhere (also where the street is not rideable, such as stairs). A way tagged lts in the .pbf file keeps that level.

Date and time

departure_datetime (and arrival_datetime in arrival_travel_time_matrix()) is read as the date and clock time it shows in its own time zone, and that clock time is taken as the local time of the 'GTFS' feeds: as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00", tz = "Europe/Paris") means 14:00 in the study area, wherever it is. It must fall on a date with service (see check_transit_availability()).

Departures and Monte Carlo draws

Without fares, a trip is routed for every departure minute of time_window and the travel times are summarised by percentiles over those departures. Routes given by frequencies (frequencies.txt) have no timetable: for each minute draws_per_minute random timetables consistent with the frequencies are drawn, so the results are a Monte Carlo sample. Give seed to make them reproducible (set.seed() has no effect on these draws); with timetables only, the draws change nothing.

With a fare_structure (see setup_fare_structure()) public transport is routed with the multi-criteria router (McRAPTOR), over time_window * draws_per_minute departure times sampled at random in the window (the same for an origin in every call with the same seed), keeping at each stop the fastest trip whose fare is within max_fare. A few numbers of draws cannot be sampled: exactly 200 departure times, or many per minute over a long window (such as 8 per minute in a 10-minute window, or 5 in a window of 150 minutes or more). Those combinations are an error.

Walking with more origins than destinations

With "WALK" alone, more origins than destinations and a network built without an elevation raster, the search runs from the destinations (fewer searches) and the columns are swapped back, taking the walk as the same in both directions. Where it is not (one-way links for pedestrians are rare, but exist) the times are those of the reverse walk. With an elevation raster, or with output_dir, the search always runs from the origins.

See also

Other routing functions: accessibility(), arrival_travel_time_matrix(), detailed_itineraries(), expanded_travel_time_matrix(), isochrone()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/spo", package = "peabiru")
network <- build_network(data_path, n_threads = 2)
points <- read.csv(file.path(data_path, "spo_points.csv"))

# walking
ttm <- travel_time_matrix(network, points, points, mode = "WALK",
                          n_threads = 2)
head(ttm)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   from_id         to_id           travel_time_p50
#>   <chr>           <chr>                     <int>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c00fffff               0
#> 2 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c007ffff               7
#> 3 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c077ffff              10
#> 4 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c03bffff               8
#> 5 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c033ffff              13
#> 6 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c0afffff              23

# public transport
ttm <- travel_time_matrix(
  network, points, points,
  mode = c("WALK", "TRANSIT"),
  departure_datetime = as.POSIXct("2019-05-13 14:00:00",
                                  tz = "America/Sao_Paulo"),
  percentiles = c(25, 50, 75),
  seed = 42,
  n_threads = 2
)
head(ttm)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   from_id         to_id          travel_time_p25 travel_time_p50 travel_time_p75
#>   <chr>           <chr>                    <int>           <int>           <int>
#> 1 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c00fff…               0               0               0
#> 2 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c007ff…               7               7               7
#> 3 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c077ff…              10              10              10
#> 4 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c03bff…               8               8               8
#> 5 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c033ff…              13              13              13
#> 6 89a8100c00fffff 89a8100c0afff…              23              23              23
